text: P1: Within one legal entity, an identifier value SHALL NOT appear more than once on the record, regardless of identifier type

comments.text: P1 constrains duplicates only within a single record, but the Intent says the register exists so callers can "reference a legal entity by identifier rather than by free text" — that resolution is ambiguous if two different LegalEntity rows carry the same LEI value, since both would be valid targets for an IssuerName or CreditSupportProviderElection ref. ISO 17442 / GLEIF treat an LEI as globally unique. Either add a requirement (and criterion) that an LEI-typed identifier value must be unique across all LegalEntity records, or state explicitly in Scope or Open Questions that cross-entity duplicates are permitted and why (e.g. pre-GLEIF legacy entities under OTHER). As written, the spec is silent on the one duplicate case that matters most for a reference register.

text: A4 (verifies P2): WHEN the identifier-type picker is rendered, THEN it SHALL offer exactly BIC, LEI, MIC, REDID, COUNTRY_CODE, OTHER and no other value.

comments.text: A4 verifies P2 only through the picker's rendering, but the observer sheet is the entity's only remote surface and accepts writes too — a save with type "XYZ" through it would pass A4 while storing a value outside the CDM EntityIdentifierTypeEnum set. Consider adding a save-time criterion for P2 (WHEN a legal entity is saved with an identifier whose type is not one of the six enum values, THEN the system SHALL reject the save) so P2 is enforced on stored data, not just on the form's dropdown.

text: a self-contained inline SVG (hexagonal node-graph mark beside the letters CDM, drawn with currentColor so it follows the theme in light and dark mode)

comments.text: The UI section drifted into HOW: it prescribed the emblem's drawing technique (inline SVG, hexagonal mark, currentColor) — a purely decorative mark whose internals belong in the ui.defaultForm artifact, where they would have to be kept in sync by hand. Trimmed to the WHAT: a decorative theme-following "CDM" emblem centered above both sections, carrying no data and no interaction.
